label: input token k at original position 1 or 2
explanation: Fires when the input token is k at the second or third original step (t = 1 or 2); it fires on essentially every such step and almost nowhere else. Magnitude depends on position: at t=1 activations are high (about 0.83-1.0 of max, highest after a leading i), and at t=2 they are lower (about 0.43-0.52 of max). Does not fire on k at t=0 or t>=3, on any other token, on the delimiter, or in the copy phase (only 8 stray copy-phase activations in the dev split). It does not depend on L, first_tok, or the outputs that come later.

issues: Minor: the 5 test-split misses (and 8 dev-split copy-phase strays) form a small but systematic class. In each, L=3 and original token 1 is k. At copy step 5 (recall_idx 2) the model's own fed-back output is the copy of original token 1, so the input is k again. Activation is very weak there (0.03-0.10 of max, 0.0% of mass). This is negligible noise, not a refutation.

Magnitude claim checks out. Activity counts at t=1 and t=2 are nearly equal (16414 vs 16861), but t=1 carries 64% of the activation mass versus 36% for t=2, so t=1 activations are roughly 1.8x larger. That matches the stated 0.83-1.0 vs 0.43-0.52 of max.

Test split: precision 1.0, recall 0.99985, F1 0.99993, mass recall 0.99999, zero false positives. The reported value of exactly 1 was rounded up slightly but is effectively correct. The feature never fires at the delimiter or at t=0 or t>=3 in the original phase, and never fires on any token other than k.
